newsitem.title: USA: Owens Corning builds fibre plant in India.
newsitem.headline: Owens Corning builds fibre plant in India.

text.p: Owens Corning has started building a plant to make composite fibre in India in a $100 million joint-venture with Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd, a local tractor and jeep maker.
Glen Hiner, the company's chairman and chief executive officer, told Reuters on Tuesday the plant in Bombay was to begin operating sometime in 1998.
"It's going to make the fibres for India and for export (to neighboring countries)," said Hiner, who was participating in a news conference to launch a national advertizing campaign for the company.
He did not immediately have the production capacity of the plant.

Hiner also said Owens Corning, a leading U.S. insulation and buidling materials maker, expected two new plants in China to begin producing insulation and rigid forms by the second quarter of next year.
Construction of the plant that will make insulation in Shanghai is to end by the first quarter of 1997, he said, adding that the cost of the project was between $15 million and $20 million.
Hiner said the plant would begin producing 8,000 tons a year with the possibility of increasing its output to 15,000 tons in two years.
The other plant in Nanjing is to be completed sometime in the second quarter of next year, he said, explaining that its cost and production capacity would be the same as the first plant.
Owens Corning is spending between $3 million and $5 million on a national advertising campaign to promote its new "System Thinking" business strategy.

The campaign, which begins Thursday and lasts until next spring, is to encourage customers to consider buying its insulation and building materials as a package when they build or remodel their homes.
It is also to provide solutions and other information to help them in improving their homes.
"We are packaging them simply and clearly for the customers to understand," said David Brown, the company's vice president, who also attended the news conference.
Brown told Reuters the strategy would help the company meet its goal of $5 billion in yearly sales by 1999.
